fastapi-02.phase_d_change: unchanged (still FALSE) -- but the reported file-level hit is now a false positive worth flagging
fastapi-02.notes: PHASE D RESULT: still a complete miss on the actual entity (fastapi.routing.APIRoute is rank 60 of 4529, score 15.47, nowhere near retrieval). The raw file-level metric shows 'hit'/recall=1.0/precision=1.0 because the one entity that did clear the threshold, APIRouter.__init__ (30.04), happens to live in the same file (routing.py) -- but APIRouter and APIRoute are two different classes; this is name-similarity coincidence, not a real match. Flagged explicitly since it's a concrete illustration of the benchmark spec's own warning that file-level recall can look better than entity-level correctness actually is (same caveat already documented for flask-06).

fastapi-03.phase_d_change: REGRESSED (was TRUE through baseline+Phase B, now FALSE)
fastapi-03.notes: PHASE D RESULT: a real regression, root-caused rather than left unexplained. fastapi.param_functions.Depends is not matched by search()'s exact_name tier for this query (that tier requires the full query string to equal an entity's name verbatim -- 'Where is the Depends() function...' never does, for any query phrased as a sentence; this is pre-existing search() behavior Phase D did not touch). The baseline's TRUE verdict therefore came from Depends() ranking first under raw cosine similarity, not from an exact-name match despite the original note's label. Under BM25, Depends() drops to rank 19 of 1778 (score 29.58 -- again just above the confidence threshold, but outside the top_k=10 window), overtaken by FastAPI/APIRouter HTTP-verb decorator methods (get/post/options/...) whose docstrings apparently share more BM25-weighted terms with this query than Depends()'s own short docstring does. A concrete, verified instance of the same top_k=10-window issue found in flask-08/fastapi-01, not a new failure mode.
